extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent applicants/practitioners (especially design patent practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Form-paragraph guidance and substantive examination standards from the MPEP addressing establishing assignee ownership, terminal disclaimers, drawing requirements, ornamentality, and statutory rejections for design patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing ownership by assignee (37 CFR 3.73 / 3.73 pre-AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership is established by submitting a signed statement identifying the assignee, accompanied by either (i) documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee (e.g., copy of an executed assignment) or (ii) a statement specifying where documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee is recorded in the assignment records of the Office (e.g., reel and frame number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The establishment of ownership by the assignee may be combined with the paper that requests or takes the action. For patent matters, documentary evidence must be accompanied by a statement affirming that the documentary evidence was, or concurrently is being, submitted for recordation pursuant to § 3.11. For trademark matters the documents may be required to be recorded as a condition to permitting the assignee to take action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee of less than entire interest must show extent
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission is by an assignee of less than the entire right, title and interest the Office may refuse to accept the submission as an establishment of ownership unless each assignee establishes the extent (by percentage) of its ownership interest so as to account for the entire right, title and interest in the application or patent by all parties including inventors; or each assignee submits a statement identifying the parties including inventors who together own the entire right, title and interest and stating that all the identified parties own the entire right, title and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple assignees exist, the Office may require delineation by percentage or an identification statement covering all parties. If two or more purported assignees file conflicting statements, the Director will determine which purported assignees will be permitted to control prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and authorization for ownership submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission establishing ownership must show that the person signing the submission is a person authorized to act on behalf of the assignee by: (1) including a statement that the person is authorized; (2) being signed by a person having apparent authority to sign on behalf of the assignee; or (3) for patent matters only, being signed by a practitioner of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should ensure signature shows authorization. Apparent authority examples include an officer of the assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for assignee establishment (patent matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent matters only: Establishment of ownership by the assignee must be submitted prior to, or at the same time as, the paper requesting or taking action is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept an assignee's paper taking action if establishment of ownership is submitted later; requirement is prior or concurrent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence recordation affirmation (37 CFR 3.73 enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission of the documentary evidence must be accompanied by a statement affirming that the documentary evidence of the chain of title from the original owner to the assignee was, or concurrently is being, submitted for recordation pursuant to § 3.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the documentary evidence is submitted but not accompanied by the required statement or not recorded among the assignment records, the assignment document may be unacceptable to satisfy 37 CFR 3.73 (use form paragraph 14.34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer fee not required twice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant (or patent owner) is not required to pay another disclaimer fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(d) when submitting a replacement or supplemental terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 14.35 (or 14.35.01 for patent owner) to notify applicant/owner. For refunds see paragraph 14.36 / 14.36.01; do not use refund paragraph if credit was to a Deposit Account or credit card—credit that account instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund suggestion when duplicate terminal disclaimer fee paid
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the required fee for the terminal disclaimer was previously paid, applicant/patent owner may request a refund of an additional terminal disclaimer fee by submitting a written request for a refund and a copy of the Office action to Mail Stop 16, Director of the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include address and note exceptions when applicant authorized credit to a Deposit Account or credit card. Use appropriate form paragraph (14.36 for applicant, 14.36.01 for patent owner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer as remedy for obviousness-type double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer may be effective to overcome a provisional obviousness-type double patenting rejection over a pending application (37 CFR 1.321(b) and (c)) or to overcome an obviousness-type double patenting rejection over a prior patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO provides terminal disclaimer forms (including eTerminal Disclaimer). Filing date of application determines which form should be used. An eTerminal Disclaimer meeting all requirements is auto-processed and approved immediately upon submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent specification arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The following order or arrangement should be observed in framing a design patent specification: (1) Preamble stating name of the applicant, title of the design, and a brief description of the nature and intended use of the article; (2) Cross-reference to related applications; (3) Statement regarding federally sponsored research or development; (4) Description of the figure or figures of the drawing; (5) Feature description; (6) A single claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this form paragraph in an international design application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of design must correspond to article (37 CFR 1.153 / 1.1067)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of a design being claimed must correspond to the name of the article in which the design is embodied or applied to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1503.01 for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing/photograph disclosure objection
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing/photograph disclosure is objected to because [reason].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner inserts reason in bracket 1. Use when drawings/photographs fail to comply with requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement drawing sheets required; rules for amended sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrected replacement drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required in reply to the Office action to avoid abandonment. Any amended replacement drawing sheet should include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is being amended. The figure number of an amended drawing should not be labeled as amended. If a drawing figure is canceled, the figure must be removed from the replacement sheet and remaining figures renumbered with consistent changes to the brief description of the several views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all figures on a drawing sheet are canceled, a replacement sheet is not required; provide an 'Annotated Sheet' showing cancellation. Each drawing sheet submitted after filing must be labeled 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' per 37 CFR 1.121(d). If changes are not accepted by the examiner, the applicant will be informed in the next Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings/photographs rules and statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Color photographs or drawings have been submitted. If replacement drawings are submitted, showing of color in a black and white drawing is limited to symbols used to line a surface to show color (MPEP § 608.02) and must comply with written description requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112. Photographs and ink drawings are not permitted to be combined as formal drawings in one application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In any drawing lined for color, the following descriptive statement must be inserted in the specification: '--The drawing is lined for color.--' Lining entire surfaces for color may interfere with showing contours; partial lining with description or a separate view omitted color but shaded for contours may be used. Some color photographs cannot be depicted accurately by black-and-white lining symbols (e.g., multiple shades), in which case alternative techniques or separate views should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing correction required prior to appeal (Ex parte Bevan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appeal of the design claim must include the correction of the drawings approved by the examiner in accordance with Ex parte Bevan, 142 USPQ 284 (Bd. App. 1964).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph in a FINAL rejection where an outstanding drawing correction requirement has not been satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of new matter in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing new or replacement drawings, be careful to avoid introducing new matter. New matter is prohibited by 35 U.S.C. 132 and 37 CFR 1.121(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should object if replacement drawings add new matter; applicant must correct to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis for design patents (35 U.S.C. 171)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotations: (a) Whoever invents any new, original, and ornamental design for an article of manufacture may obtain a patent therefor; (b) provisions of this title relating to patents for inventions apply to patents for designs, except as otherwise provided; (c) filing date of a design application is the date on which the specification as prescribed by section 112 and any required drawings are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this statutory text (form paragraph 15.07.01) when asserting statutory basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of ornamentality rejection standard (35 U.S.C. 171)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 171 as being directed to nonstatutory subject matter in that it lacks ornamentality. To be patentable, a design must be 'created for the purpose of ornamenting' the article in which it is embodied. Evidence that demonstrates a prima facie case of a lack of ornamentality should be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence to demonstrate the design is ornamental may be submitted in the form of an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 identifying what aspects of the design meet those considerations. A representative of the company commissioning the design may submit a declaration. Attorney arguments are not a substitute for evidence (Ex parte Webb). Examiner Note: insert the source of evidence (e.g., utility patent, brochure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of ornamentality when article not visible in normal use
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 171 when the design lacks ornamentality because it appears there is no period in the commercial life of the article when its ornamentality may be a matter of concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To overcome, applicant needs two types of evidence: (1) evidence demonstrating there is some period in the commercial life when ornamentality matters (e.g., sales literature, advertisement, catalog showing appearance as ornamental), and (2) evidence demonstrating the design is ornamental (affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 stating ornamental considerations and identifying aspects of the design that meet those considerations). Representative company declarations allowed; attorney argument insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulation rejection (design merely simulating another article/person)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 171 as lacking originality where the design is merely simulating [an article or person] which applicant did not invent (e.g., White House, Marilyn Monroe, an animal not stylized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow with explanation and evidence (form paragraph 15.08.03) when evidence has been cited to show the article or person being simulated. Examiner Note: insert the name of article/person being simulated. Use representative references to show the usual appearance of the simulated item for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of evidence for simulation rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's design has in no way departed from the natural appearance of [reference]. This reference is supplied merely as representative of the usual or typical appearance of [reference] in order that the claim may be compared to that which it is simulating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claim is directed to surface treatment not shown with an article in full or broken lines. Insert reference in bracket 1 and name in bracket 2 as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offensive subject matter rejection (decorum / courtesy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure, and therefore the claim in this application, is rejected as being offensive and therefore improper subject matter for design patent protection under 35 U.S.C. 171. Such subject matter does not meet statutory requirements and 37 CFR 1.3 proscribes presentation of papers lacking in decorum and courtesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include where depictions or caricatures in disclosure/drawings/claim might reasonably be considered offensive. See MPEP § 608 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper inventorship rejection (35 U.S.C. 115)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must include the name of the inventor for any invention claimed; the present application sets forth incorrect inventorship because [reason]. The claim can be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 171 and 35 U.S.C. 115 for failing to set forth correct inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert basis for concluding inventorship is incorrect in bracket 1. Use form paragraph 15.07.01 (statutory text) before this when appropriate. Use only once in an Office action where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA First Inventor to File statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The present application, filed on or after March 16, 2013, is being examined under the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in any application subject to first-inventor-to-file provisions. Use form paragraph 15.10.aia or 15.10.fti as applicable to indicate examination regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) — anticipation (AIA / pre-AIA variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by [reference] because the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 identify the reference applied. For applications with filing dates on/after March 16, 2013 that claim priority to earlier applications, precede with form paragraphs 15.10.aia and 15.10.15 as required. Use explanation paragraph 15.15.01.aia to explain basis of rejection and compare appearances (e.g., International Seaway Trading Corp. v. Walgreens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection (more than one year before filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as being anticipated by [reference] because the invention was patented or described in a printed publication, or was in public use or on sale in this country more than one (1) year prior to the application for patent in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert identifying reference in bracket 1. For applications subject to pre-AIA prior art provisions, use appropriate form paragraphs and precede with 15.10.15 when priority issues across AIA/pre-AIA arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d)/35 U.S.C. 172 foreign filing anticipation
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d), as modified by pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 172, as being anticipated by [reference] because the invention was first patented or was the subject of inventor's certificate in a foreign country prior to the U.S. application where the foreign application was filed more than six (6) months before the U.S. filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert reference applied in bracket 1. Note statutory implications for design patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) AIA rejection (reference in another's earlier effective filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by [reference] because the claimed invention was described in a patent or in an application for patent published or deemed published under section 122(b) in which the patent or application names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the reference in bracket 1. For claims with priority/back-bilateral priority to pre-March 16, 2013 applications, precede with form paragraphs 15.10.aia and 15.10.15 as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of appearance-based rejection (substantial similarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appearance of [reference] is substantially the same as that of the claimed design (see International Seaway Trading Corp. v. Walgreens Corp.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 15.15.01.aia (or 15.15.01.fti for pre-AIA) to explain the basis of the rejection and identify the reference applied. Insert the reference in bracket 1.
